 Riley Meredith to return to Somerset for 2027 season
 Somerset CCC 
 Cricket 
 Sport 
 Somerset 
 By 
 Dan Wilkins
 Audience & Content Editor 
 Share
 0 Comments 
 Riley Meredith celebrating a wicket with his Somerset teammates (Image: Somerset CCC) 
 This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today,
 and has been written by our American colleagues.
 It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.
 Australian fast bowler Riley Meredith is set to return to Somerset for the 2027 season.
 He will be available for the full Vitality Blast campaign, after helping Somerset lift the T20 title in 2025 as their leading wicket-taker.
 Meredith said: "I’m looking forward to coming back to Somerset.
 "There’s a really good group of guys in the dressing room and it’s a great place to play.
 "I’ve loved my time in Taunton because it’s a great club to be a part of.
 "Hopefully, we can lift that trophy again next summer."
 The 30-year-old first joined Somerset in 2024 and has since taken 56 wickets in 34 T20 matches at an average of 17.94.
 Andy Hurry, Somerset’s director of cricket, said: "Riley is one of those players who genuinely makes spectators get up off their seats.
 "He possesses genuine pace, constantly asks questions of batters and brings a little bit of X-factor to our attack.
 "He has played a pivotal role in our T20 success over the last three seasons, and we are confident that he will positively contribute again in 2027."
